text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- German property fund CGI buys centre of Amsterdam suburb Amstelveen for 650 million guilders. (p1)
- Financial services group Moret Ernst and Young Nederland mulls changing partnership structure. (p1)
- Group of options traders crank up the price of AEX shares by Dfl 80 million. (p1)
- Majority of EU members accept Dutch proposal for intergovernmental conference which must lead to June summit. (p1)
- Industrial group Begemann talks with Malaysian carmaker Proton about sale of automatic transmission unit VCST. (p3)
- Malaysian delegation visits Fokker to talk about participation in aircraft maker's relaunch. (p3)
- Entertainment group Endemol takes 49 pct stake in Germany's TV company GAT-film + TV Production. (p4)
- Builder HBG sees flat result in 1997 despite doubling turnover through acquisitions. (p3)
VOLKSKRANT
- Christian Democrats party choose Jaap de Hoop Scheffer to head the list of candidates for next year's election. (p1)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm looks for legal means to ban pyramid schemes. (p1)
- Publisher Elsevier's managers earned 25 million guilders from exercising options. (p2)
- Telecom company Libertel to sharpen its competition with KPN PTT Telecom. (p2)
DDE TELEGRAAF
- Bank robber holds five people hostage for ten hours before surrendering. (p1)
- Dutch transporters furious about Spain's ban on driving for trucks. (p3)
- EU team investigates Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM head office following cut-price airline Easy Jet complaints. (p25)
- Textile company Ten Cate to continue restructuring. (p25)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Top civil servant says money spent on environment useless because it does not create jobs or improve infrastructure. (p1)
TROUW
- Companies threaten to stop sponsoring football if violence does not stop. (p1)
- Temp agency Randstad sees 1996 profit grow 27 percent to Dfl 207.4 million. (p7)
